A regime applicable only to corporate taxpayers
The default regime with limited or no exemptions and deductions
An optional regime with all deductions and exemptions available

s: Under the new tax regime from Budget 2025-26, income in the slab of ₹20–24 lakh and income above ₹24 lakh are taxed respectively at:

s:
Consider the following statements regarding the new tax regime:
1. Income up to ₹12 lakh is made tax-free through the Section 87A rebate.
2. For a salaried individual, the corresponding limit is ₹12.75 lakh when the standard deduction is taken into account.
3. The standard deduction relevant to this limit is ₹75,000.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: All three statements are correct: the Section 87A rebate makes income up to ₹12 lakh tax-free, and the ₹75,000 standard deduction raises the effective salaried threshold to ₹12.75 lakh.
tq: Check whether the rebate threshold, salaried threshold and deduction amount form one consistent set.

s: Which one of the following statements correctly describes the change in the highest surcharge under the new tax regime introduced in Budget 2023-24?
o: It was reduced from 37% to 25% for income above ₹2 crore
It was increased from 25% to 37% for income above ₹2 crore
It was reduced from 30% to 20% for income above ₹5 crore
It was abolished for income above ₹2 crore

s:
Which of the following statements regarding the successive new-regime tax structures is correct?
1. The Budget 2020-21 regime began with a nil slab up to ₹2.5 lakh.
2. Budget 2023-24 introduced a nil slab up to ₹3 lakh.
3. Budget 2026-27 made no change in the slabs applicable from Budget 2025-26.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: All three statements are correct. The initial regime had a nil slab up to ₹2.5 lakh, the 2023-24 structure raised it to ₹3 lakh, and Budget 2026-27 retained the 2025-26 slabs.
tq: Compare the nil-slab thresholds across the three Budgets instead of treating the regimes as identical.
sec: Income tax regimes - slabs, rebate, standard deduction, surcharge  [APPSC]

s:
Arrange the following changes in the new tax regime in chronological order:
A. Income up to ₹12 lakh became tax-free through rebate.
B. A new optional tax regime with a nil slab up to ₹2.5 lakh was introduced.
C. The nil slab was revised to ₹3 lakh and the highest surcharge was reduced to 25%.
D. No change was made in the slabs introduced in Budget 2025-26.
x: The sequence is Budget 2020-21, Budget 2023-24, Budget 2025-26 and Budget 2026-27: B, C, A, D.
tq: Fix the first and last Budget before ordering the intermediate reforms.
sec: Income tax regimes - slabs, rebate, standard deduction, surcharge  [APPSC]

s: Which one of the following is correct regarding the old income-tax regime?
o: It continues as an optional regime with deductions and exemptions
It was completely abolished when the new regime became the default
It provides no deductions or exemptions
It applies only to companies opting for MAT

B. Wealth tax

D. Estate duty

2. 1957

Estate duty was abolished in 2015 and wealth tax in 1985
Wealth tax was abolished in 2015 and gift tax in October 1998
Expenditure tax continues, while estate duty was abolished in 1998

s:
Consider the following statements about the Minimum Alternate Tax (MAT):

2. The Finance Act, 1987 made it effective from assessment year 1988-89.
3. It was discontinued in 1990-91 and reintroduced in 1996-97 at an effective rate of 11.87%.

s: Minimum Alternate Tax is primarily imposed on companies which:
o: Have no book profits but earn only agricultural income
Are registered as unlisted start-ups receiving share premium
Show book profits but otherwise pay little or no regular income tax
x: MAT taxes so-called zero-tax companies on their book profits, ensuring a minimum tax liability despite low or nil regular income-tax liability.
tq: Apply the purpose of the tax to a company’s accounting and regular-tax situation.

s: With reference to MAT under Budget 2026-27, which one of the following is correct?
o: The rate was raised to 18% and all MAT credit was cancelled
The rate remained 15% and new MAT credit continued without restriction
The rate was reduced to 14%, made a final tax, and no new MAT credit is allowed after 1 April 2026
MAT was abolished for all companies from 1 April 2026
x: Budget 2026-27 reduced MAT to 14% and made it a final tax; no new MAT credit is available after 1 April 2026.
tq: Separate the rate change from the change in the nature of tax and MAT-credit treatment.

s: Which one of the following correctly states the treatment of old MAT credit under Budget 2026-27?
o: It may be set off only under the old regime without any ceiling
It may be set off up to one-fourth of the liability only under the new regime
It cannot be set off under either regime
It may be set off against the entire tax liability under every regime
x: Old MAT credit can be set off up to 25%—one-fourth—of the liability and only for taxpayers under the new regime.
tq: Check both restrictions: the one-fourth ceiling and the applicable regime.

A capital gain arises on transfer such as sale, exchange or relinquishment of a capital asset
A capital gain arises on every purchase of a capital asset
A capital gain arises only when an asset is held for more than 24 months

Securities Transaction Tax payable only by stock exchanges

1. It advocated lower tax rates and a broader tax base.
2. It was associated with the revision of wealth tax in 1992.
3. It recommended increasing the number of tax exemptions.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: The Committee advocated lower rates, a broader base and fewer exemptions, and formed the basis of the 1992 wealth-tax revision. Statement 3 is false because it favoured fewer exemptions.

s:
Which of the following statements regarding the FAST-DS 2026 is correct?
1. It concerns foreign assets of small taxpayers.
2. It was announced in Budget 2026–27 and came into force on 16 August 2026.
3. Declarations can be filed up to 31 December 2026.

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: FAST-DS means Foreign Assets of Small Taxpayers—Disclosure Scheme. It was announced in Budget 2026–27, came into force on 16 August 2026, and permits declarations up to 31 December 2026.
tq: Combine the scheme name, commencement date and filing deadline.
sec: Black money disclosure schemes

s: Under FAST-DS 2026, which of the following correctly states the tax structure and asset threshold?
o: 30% tax plus an equal additional amount; ₹1 crore generally and ₹5 crore for previously taxed but unreported assets
50% levy; ₹5 crore generally and ₹1 crore for previously taxed assets
45% total levy; ₹1 crore generally and ₹5 crore for all foreign assets
15% tax without an additional amount; ₹1 crore for all declarations
x: FAST-DS imposes 30% tax plus an equal additional amount, producing an effective 60% burden. The threshold is ₹1 crore, rising to ₹5 crore for previously taxed but unreported assets.
tq: Split the option into rate and threshold before selecting the complete pair.
sec: Black money disclosure schemes

s: Which of the following is correctly associated with FAST-DS 2026?
o: A ₹1 lakh fee applies to previously taxed but unreported assets, and fair market value is taken as on 31 March 2026.
The scheme applies to domestic assets valued as on 1 April 2025.
A ₹1 lakh fee applies to every declaration, and valuation is as on 31 December 2026.
The scheme grants immunity only from civil liability under the Income-tax Act.
x: For previously taxed but unreported assets, FAST-DS provides a ₹1 lakh fee and uses fair market value as on 31 March 2026. It also provides immunity from penalty and prosecution under the Black Money Act, 2015.
tq: Use the valuation date and fee as high-precision identifiers.
sec: Black money disclosure schemes

s: The statutory basis specifically dealing with undisclosed foreign income and assets and imposition of tax is the:
o: Direct Tax Vivad se Vishwas Act, 2020
Black Money (Undisclosed Foreign Income and Assets) and Imposition of Tax Act, 2015

tq: Identify the statute from its exact subject-matter title.

s: The Vodafone tax dispute led to which of the following developments?
o: A 50% levy under PMGKY after demonetisation
A retrospective amendment in 2012 relating to indirect transfers, followed by withdrawal of retrospective demands in 2021
A 2016 levy on online advertising followed by its abolition in 2025
A 15% global minimum corporate tax under OECD Pillar Two
x: Following the Supreme Court's 2012 Vodafone ruling, indirect transfers were taxed retrospectively through the Finance Act, 2012. The Taxation Laws (Amendment) Act, 2021 withdrew the retrospective demands involving Vodafone and Cairn.
tq: Track the legal sequence rather than confusing it with a digital levy.
